          All-Action Ronald Araújo Looks Right at Home at Liverpool
        
      
                          
                      Oct 27, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Some eyebrows were raised when Liverpool signed Ronald Araújo on loan from Barcelona this summer, but he is more than justifying the faith shown in him by Andoni Iraola.
They say you should never fall in love with a loan player.
Like a library book or a rental car, you simply can’t get too attached when the agreement is only short-term.
However, the Anfield crowd couldn’t help themselves on Sunday. Ronald Araújo was just too endearing.
Two main things fans want to see from their players are ability and passion, and when those are combined to lead to victory, there’s not much more that can be asked for.

Liverpool were unsurprisingly made to work hard for their 2-0 win by in-form Brighton & Hove Albion, and their pair of first-half goals were cheered raucously. First came a Pascal Groß own goal forced by Florian Wirtz’s shot, and then Alexander Isak buried Bradley Barcola’s cross as the ruthless Reds raced into a two-goal lead after just 21 minutes.

But those decibels were almost equalled in the second half as Araújo set about tackling Brighton players in an almost comically aggressive but successful fashion to ensure Liverpool’s sheet remained clean and that their first three points in a home league game this season were collected.

That was after the Uruguayan had produced a moment that later went viral in the first half when he blocked a shot from Maxim De Cuyper, before taking the choice while still on the floor to tackle his opponent with his head. It was a moment enjoyed by everyone associated with Liverpool, except perhaps for the medical team who may have broken out in a cold sweat at Araújo's flagrant disregard for keeping his head un-kicked.
Ronald giving EVERYTHING to secure the clean sheet 💪😅 pic.twitter.com/lPNASzhw22

It was another solid outing for Araújo, who had more touches than any other Liverpool player in the game (59), won possession six times – only Alexis Mac Allister (7) did so more often for the hosts – and made eight clearances, second only to Virgil van Dijk (10).

Araújo was something of a surprise signing from Barcelona in the summer. Liverpool rarely pick up players on loan, and bringing in a 27-year-old defender for just one year seemed unusually knee-jerk for a club who usually pride themselves on long-term planning.

That said, it wasn’t entirely without justification. Araújo had been captain at Camp Nou, came with plenty of top-level experience, and he largely impressed during his time in Spain. He did struggle with form last season, culminating in a red card in Barcelona’s defeat at Chelsea in the Champions League. Following that game, the player decided to take a break to work on improving his mental health.

In a recent interview with The Times, Araújo opened up on what was “a very difficult time,” adding: “I felt that what I needed to do was take a step back. I hadn’t felt right for a long time, and I wasn’t enjoying the thing I love most, which is football.

“I realised I had to put my hand up, ask for help and talk not just to the people closest to me, but to professionals as well. Sometimes you bottle things up and try to be the strong man, but in life you have to talk about things and open up about what you’re going through.”
If his early form for Liverpool is anything to go by, that break and fresh surroundings have been exactly the tonic Araújo needed.

When you sign a player from Barcelona, you don’t necessarily expect to receive a blood-and-thunder type, but many who had watched Araújo closely in La Liga did suggest he may suit the Premier League given the more physical style of play. That appears to have been spot on, as he has warmed to things quickly England, and it is really benefitting Andoni Iraola and Liverpool.

His new boss has shown plenty of faith in him even though he’s only a loan player. Araújo is one of only three players to have featured in all 12 of Liverpool’s games this season along with Jérémy Jacquet and Mac Allister.

One of the reasons he has had so many opportunities is his versatility. Araújo was predominantly a centre-back for Barcelona, but he has played more than three quarters of his minutes for Liverpool this season at right-back (76%). The long-term injury to Conor Bradley and the form/fitness of Jeremie Frimpong opened up a spot in the back four, and Araújo has filled it seamlessly.

He is providing extra strength and defensive nous for Liverpool, who at times last season looked like they were a bit too easy to play against, but there hasn’t had to be much compromise in terms of attacking output. Araújo has two goals and an assist in his 12 games, with all three of his goal involvements coming in the Champions League.

He produced a cheeky assist for Dominik Szoboszlai in the home win over Atlético Madrid, backheeling the ball to the Hungarian to score, while he headed in the opener in the 6-3 victory in LASK, and then grabbed an equaliser in the 4-3 success over Villarreal last week.
